service.description: A record's place on a map, for the local-map dialog and a record layer's drill-down: its label, geometry, precision and source, the version a later store#RecordLocation names, what the caller may do and where the record's links go. The adapter checks the caller's access to the record first; a record the caller may not read, or that is not there, answers only reasonCode (PERMISSION_DENIED or RECORD_UNAVAILABLE) and nothing of the record, so the two are told apart by no one but the adapter. Reads change nothing: no address is rewritten, no point saved, no outside service asked.

parameter.name: recordKey
parameter.description: The record's canonical identity, its primary key fields ({partyId}, {facilityId}); the adapter reads only the keys it knows

parameter.name: addressPurpose
parameter.description: Which of the record's locations, where it has several (a mailing address, a delivery entrance): the adapter's own purpose id; empty for its default

parameter.name: label
parameter.description: Plain text, escaped where it is shown

parameter.name: geometry
parameter.description: A GeoJSON geometry; null when the record has no location the adapter can give

parameter.name: extent
parameter.description: A broad extent where the position is approximate (a postal area), so the map does not zoom to a point it does not know

parameter.name: precisionEnumId
parameter.description: GeoPointPrecision: user-confirmed, address match, street range, postal area or place estimate

parameter.name: sourceText
parameter.description: Where the position came from, in words (a data set and its edition, a user's confirmation and when)

parameter.name: recordVersion
parameter.description: The version read (a lastUpdatedStamp, a revision, an address fingerprint), handed back to store#RecordLocation

parameter.name: permittedActions
parameter.description: What the caller may do here, of: view, chooseLocation (only when store#RecordLocation would permit the write)

parameter.name: links
parameter.description: Each {label, route, parameters}: route a key the application showing the map resolves, never a URL

parameter.name: reasonCode
parameter.description: Set, with nothing else, when the record is not shown

parameter.name: postalCode
parameter.description: With no geometry: the postal code of the record's address, so the map shows its local postal-area position (get#PostalLocation, approximate, with a broad extent) and no outside service is asked; never a substitute for a recorded point

parameter.name: countryGeoId
parameter.description: The country of postalCode: a Geo ID or an ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 code

parameter.name: address1
parameter.description: With no geometry: the address's street line (number and street), which the installation's local geocoder (MPK_GEOCODER_OVERTURE, this server's own index, no outside request) matches when one is enabled, before the postal area; the point found is shown, never saved

parameter.name: address2
parameter.description: Its second line, used only when it names a unit (Apt, Suite, #)

parameter.name: city
parameter.description: Its locality

service.description: Save a location a user chose for a record (Choose location in the local-map dialog). The adapter checks again that the caller may write this record, that recordVersion is still the record's and that its address is the one shown, and saves through its domain's guarded services with provenance. A refusal a person can act on (a changed record, no right to write) is answered: applied false, with reasonCode (STALE_VERSION, PERMISSION_DENIED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE) and reason. A postal fallback never replaces a recorded facility or asset point; the widget cannot issue any other entity update.

parameter.name: recordVersion
parameter.description: The version get#RecordMapContext answered

parameter.name: point
parameter.description: {longitude, latitude}, WGS84, each in range

parameter.name: recordVersion
parameter.description: The record's version after the save

service.description: The features of a record layer within a viewport, bounded: at most limit, which the caller has bounded by maps@max-features (get#AdapterService), and truncated true when there were more. The adapter applies the caller's permissions and organization scope to the query itself, on every viewport; a feature carries only what the caller may read (no hidden attribute for the browser to filter out), and never a whole table.

parameter.name: layerId
parameter.description: The MapLayer asked for, for an adapter that serves more than one

parameter.name: extent
parameter.description: {west, south, east, north}, WGS84

parameter.name: features
parameter.description: Each {featureId, label, geometry, precisionEnumId, links}, as get#RecordMapContext's

service.description: The registered map adapters (moqui.maps.MapAdapter) in order, each with its operations (context, store, features) and service names, for the server's own callers: a screen gives a browser the key, description and operations, never a service name. A disabled row is left out, and so is a row naming a service that does not exist or does not take the in-parameters of the interface it stands for (the implements of its definition), or naming none of context and features, which is logged by name: one bad registration never takes the others with it. adapterKey narrows the list to that adapter.

iterate.script: adapterList.push({ adapterKey: row.adapterKey, description: row.description ? ec.l10n.localize(row.description) : row.adapterKey, operations: [ row.contextServiceName ? "context" : null, row.storeServiceName ? "store" : null, row.featuresServiceName ? "features" : null ].filter(operation => operation), contextServiceName: row.contextServiceName || null, storeServiceName: row.storeServiceName || null, featuresServiceName: row.featuresServiceName || null })

service.description: The service that carries out operation (context: get#RecordMapContext, store: store#RecordLocation, features: find#LayerFeatures) for the adapter registered as adapterKey, for a browser-facing transition or service that has only the key the browser sent. An error for a key that is not registered (or was left out by find#MapAdapters) and for an operation the adapter does not offer. For features, limit is the count to pass on: the one asked for, at most maps@max-features, which it is when none is asked for; a maps@max-features that is not a whole number is logged and the features operation refused, with no number of the code's own in its place.

parameter.name: operation
parameter.description: context, store or features

parameter.name: limit
parameter.description: For features: the count asked for

parameter.name: adapter
parameter.description: {adapterKey, description, operations}

return.message: No map adapter is registered as ${adapterKey}

log.message: maps@max-features is not a whole number (${maxFeaturesText}): no features are read

return.message: Map features are not available: maps@max-features is not a whole number

set.from: limit == null || limit > maxFeatures ? maxFeatures : Math.max(limit, 0)

service.description: The configuration a map draws (m-map's, WebrootMap.js), for a map-view's config-url and the Maps screens. Precedence (plans/archive/Maps.md §4.2): the installation's policy (maps@external-requests: false leaves out every profile, basemap and layer drawn from an outside host) constrains every choice; the profile is the one asked for (profileId, the consumer's), else the user's own maps.profile preference, else their groups' (the ALL_USERS one is the installation's default), else OUTLINE; the user's maps.preferences (basemap, layer visibility, initial extent, the last view when they opted in, units) override the profile's defaults where its allowedOverrides permit; a record's place (adapterKey, recordKey, addressPurpose) overrides the initial viewport. A profile that is gone, disabled, not permitted (viewPermission) or not drawable falls back to the next, with an explanation in fallbacks and profile.notice; an installation without the OUTLINE row or the maps.profile preference still draws the outline, and an administrator is told so, with the link to Configuration only when they may open it. A layer that is gone, disabled, not permitted or not drawable is left out and named in layerErrors (and in fallbacks when the profile or a preference named it); one the caller may not see is, to them, one that is not there (LAYER_MISSING, PROFILE_MISSING, named by the ID asked for) unless they may open Configuration. An outside URL is handed out only of an enabled provider that passed its test as it is configured now, on its own origin (SOURCE_UNTESTED, URL_NOT_PROVIDERS, PROVIDER_UNTESTED otherwise); allowedOrigins are those origins, each tile subdomain by itself. No provider's key, service, entity or resource name reaches the browser: a provider with a key is not offered at all (PROVIDER_KEYED). With adapterKey the registered adapter's get#RecordMapContext gives the record's place (points, or features for another geometry) and record (label, precision, source, version, permitted actions, links, and resolvedLinks: {label, route, url} of each link a registered MapRoute of the host app, routeApp, else of no app, resolves to a screen the user's own grants open, MapRoutes.js) after its own access check; a refusal, an adapter the user may not call and a failure are a layer error (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE for the first two, which are not told apart, ADAPTER_FAILED), never a failed configuration, and the adapter's own text is neither answered nor logged here. A record layer is listed in recordLayers; a shown one's features (find#LayerFeatures, for the initial extent) are cut to get#AdapterService's limit (maps@max-features), with featuresTruncated, and a hidden one's adapter is not asked. Changes nothing.

parameter.name: layerIds
parameter.description: Layer IDs, comma separated; empty for the profile's

parameter.name: recordKey
parameter.description: The record's key fields, a map or its JSON

parameter.name: routeApp
parameter.description: The app showing the map (its mount of LocalMap passes it): a record's links resolve to its MapRoute rows first, then to those of no app, never to another app's

parameter.name: featuresExtent
recordLayers
parameter.description: false: the record layers are listed and no adapter is asked for their features (the local-map dialog, which shows one record)

parameter.name: locationShares
parameter.description: true: the configuration carries locationShares (plans/Location-Sharing.md §3.3), the caller's own active shares and those shared with them now, read only through LocationServices find#MyShares, find#SharedWithMe and get#Share, which check the caller against each share's current audience: Maps › Browse's getConfig asks for them (its terminal twin reads the same through MapConfig.js liveShares), a map-view's config-url and the local-map dialog do not; with locationSharesFailed true when one of those reads failed

parameter.name: config
parameter.description: {profileId, profile: {profileId, profileName, basemaps, basemap, allowedOrigins, notice}, layers, recordLayers, center, zoom, extent, units, points, features, featuresTruncated, record, fallbacks: [{kind, id, reasonCode, message}], layerErrors: [{id, label, reasonCode, message}], externalRequests, and with locationShares: locationShares [{shareId, role (owner or viewer), label, ownerName (a viewer's), purposeText, fromDate, thruDate (epoch millis), approximate, keepTrail, latest {latitude, longitude, accuracy, heading, speed, observedDate, ageSeconds} or null, trail [[longitude, latitude]] (its latest 500 points, of at most 10 shares, when kept), and an owner's trailKeepDays, trailCount, audience [{audienceSeqId, audienceTypeEnumId, userGroupId, name}] and reportIntervalSeconds}]}

service.description: The signed-in user's map preferences: their own default profile (UserPreference maps.profile, null for the installation's), and from maps.preferences (theirs, else their groups') the basemap, initial extent, units, whether the last view is restored (and it, when so) and each layer's visibility; with the profiles and basemaps they may choose from (enabled, permitted and drawable under the outside-request policy) and the installation's default profile.

Change the signed-in user's map preferences: each parameter given replaces its preference, an empty one clears it, one not given is kept. The profile (maps.profile) and the basemap must be ones the user may be offered, an enabled and permitted profile whose basemap's provider is enabled and an enabled provider's basemap, so a preference never turns on a provider an administrator has not approved (PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE, BASEMAP_UNAVAILABLE, LAYER_UNAVAILABLE, with the cause); a malformed extent, units or last view is an error. The last view is kept only while restoreLastView is on; turning it off clears it.

parameter.name: extent
parameter.description: west, south, east, north in degrees (a list or a comma text)

parameter.name: units
parameter.description: metric or imperial; empty for the profile's or the locale's

parameter.name: lastView
parameter.description: {center: [lon, lat], zoom}

parameter.name: layers
parameter.description: {layerId: true or false}

parameter.name: rasters
parameter.description: A COG layer's band settings by its ID (P4c): {layerId: {rgb: [r, g, b] or band, min, max, colormap (grey, viridis, terrain, magma), nodata}}, each band one of the layer's; a layer's null clears its settings (RASTER_INVALID for one that does not read)

service.description: The saved map views the signed-in user may read: their own and those others shared, by name, at most 500, narrowed to a profile. Each has its view (center and zoom or extent, projection, basemap, layers), whether it is the user's own and shared, and its owner's name; a layer or basemap of it the reader may not be offered is left out, with an explanation.

Save a map view: a new one (no savedViewId) owned by the signed-in user, or a change of one of theirs. Another user's view is refused (PERMISSION_DENIED for a shared one, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE for a private one or one that is not there, which are not told apart). The view's extent, center, zoom and projection are checked, and its profile, basemap and layers must be ones the owner may be offered (PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE, BASEMAP_UNAVAILABLE, LAYER_UNAVAILABLE). Private unless isShared; at most 500 a user (TOO_MANY_VIEWS).

parameter.name: isShared
parameter.description: Y or N (true or false)

parameter.name: view
parameter.description: {center, zoom} or {extent}, with projection, basemap and layers; a map or its JSON

service.description: Delete one of the signed-in user's saved map views; another user's is refused as store#SavedView refuses it.

What Maps › Configuration shows, for a caller who may open it (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise): each map profile (enabled, the installation's default, whether it can be drawn now and why not) and each layer (its provider, whether a basemap or a record layer, enabled, drawable and why not), at most 200 of each, and the installation's outside-request policy and limits as the conf sets them (maps@external-requests, maps@max-features, maps@import-max-bytes), which are changed only in the conf. Changes nothing.

The map projection registry (P4c, MapProjection) for Maps › Configuration › Projections: each row with its definition, axis order, area of use, extent, whether it is enabled and whether the server reads its definition (check#ProjectionDefinition: overlays in it are converted and a COG's bounds known) or only a browser draws it, with the reason. For a caller who may open Configuration (their own grant; PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise).

Add or change a map projection (P4c, MapProjection), or enable or disable one (only projectionId and disabled given), for a caller who may change Maps › Configuration (their own grant; PERMISSION_DENIED). The code is an EPSG code other than EPSG:4326 and EPSG:3857 (every map's own); the definition PROJ.4 text of plain parameters (no URL, no grid but +nadgrids=@null), which a browser registers with proj4 (DEFINITION_INVALID otherwise); the area of use west, south, east, north in degrees; the extent four numbers in its units. The answer says whether the server reads it too (serverReadable, serverReason): one it does not is still drawn by a map, and an overlay in it is refused with that reason.

parameter.name: bounds
parameter.description: west,south,east,north in degrees

parameter.name: projectedExtent
parameter.description: minx,miny,maxx,maxy in its units; empty for none

parameter.name: disabled
parameter.description: Y or N; empty to leave it

service.description: Enable or disable a map profile and make one the installation's default (the ALL_USERS UserGroupPreference maps.profile), for a caller who may open and change Maps › Configuration (its view and update; PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise). Both changes are in the audit log (MapProfile.disabled, UserGroupPreference.preferenceValue). The default must be enabled and drawable now (PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE, with the cause: a profile whose provider has not passed its test, one drawn from outside while outside requests are off); the default is not disabled (DEFAULT_PROFILE). A profile may be enabled before its provider is: it is then not drawn, and the answer says so. An unknown profile is RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

parameter.name: enabled
parameter.description: Y or N; empty to leave it

parameter.name: viewProjection
parameter.description: The projection the profile's map is drawn in (P4c): EPSG:3857 (also for empty), EPSG:4326 or a MapProjection row's code; a basemap of vector tiles is drawn only in EPSG:3857, so it is refused with another (PROJECTION_INCOMPATIBLE); not given to leave it

service.description: An OGC service's GetCapabilities text (WMS 1.3.0, WMTS 1.0.0, WFS 2.0.0), which a provider's test fetched, read by moqui-lib's XML reader (geo/ogc.rs: a DOCTYPE, an entity declaration and an unknown entity refuse it) into the JSON the provider records (capabilitiesJson; MapOgc.js). Sends and writes nothing; no group is granted it: the provider's test calls it.

parameter.name: service
parameter.description: wms, wmts or wfs

parameter.name: refused
parameter.description: Why it is not capabilities a map reads, a short fixed text

service.description: For Configuration's Add OGC layer: the OGC providers (WMS, WMTS, WFS) that passed their test as they are now, and, for one of them, what its last test recorded (capabilitiesJson): its layers or feature types, and for the layer named its styles, formats, the CRSs a map draws, its matrix sets (WMTS) and its time dimension. No request is sent. For a caller who may open Maps › Configuration (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise).

parameter.name: ogcLayers
parameter.description: The layer whose choices are asked for

service.description: A layer of a tested OGC provider (MapLayer of format MLF_WMS, MLF_WMTS or MLF_WFS), from what its last test recorded: the layer or layers (a WMS may name several), style, format, CRS, matrix set (WMTS), time and whether a WMS layer is one image of the view. It is checked as a map draws it before it is kept (LAYER_UNAVAILABLE, with the cause: a name, style, format, CRS or matrix set its capabilities do not have). A WMS or WMTS layer may be a basemap; a WFS layer is an overlay. With a profileId an overlay is also added to that profile's layers, shown, and a basemap becomes that profile's basemap. For a caller who may open and change Maps › Configuration (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise); PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE for a provider that is not a tested OGC one.

One operation (list, get, store, test, consumers) of the mapProvider connection kind (a ConnectionAdapter row, data/AdminConfigurationData.xml), whose native record is moqui.maps.MapProvider, for org.moqui.admin.ConfigurationServices: the name, kind, style or tile URL, attribution and its links and terms URL change here, the key (apiKey) is write-only, and whether the server may reach the provider on its own network is shown and changed only in Tools. The engine's rules hold: a change of the URL or the kind clears the key and disables the provider until a test passes, and a provider is enabled only after a passing test of its configuration as it is. The test is one GET with no credentials, following no redirect and reading at most 2 MB (a style document must parse and name only its own origin; a raster template must answer an image; a raster provider whose URL is a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF, a .tif or .tiff path with no tile placeholder, as a bucket of COGs has, is read as registering one of its COGs reads it: one range of its first 64 KiB, a 206 this site may read by CORS, its header one a map draws, never through the proxy or with a key), to no internal address unless the private network is allowed; an archive provider has no URL (ARCHIVE_ENDPOINT). While maps@external-requests is false a provider is neither tested nor enabled (EXTERNAL_REQUESTS_OFF). Needs ADMIN_CONNECTION_VIEW to read and ADMIN_CONNECTION_MANAGE to change or test; no group is authorized to call it directly.

The Maps readiness providers (data/AdminConfigurationData.xml), answering the readiness contract's checks and changing nothing. maps.profile (ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW): the installation's default profile is set and can be drawn (DEFAULT_PROFILE_UNSET, or the profile's reason), and the outline fallback (informational OUTLINE_IN_USE, or OUTLINE_MISSING). maps.providers (ADMIN_CONNECTION_VIEW): a layer that asks an outside host with no provider is not drawn (SOURCE_UNTESTED); each enabled provider's last test passed for its configuration as it is (TEST_FAILED, UNTESTED), one with a key is not drawn (PROVIDER_KEYED), each is offered while outside requests are allowed (EXTERNAL_REQUESTS_OFF), and the page's Content-Security-Policy (the screen-render header and webapp@csp-append) lets a browser reach its origins, each tile subdomain, in connect-src, img-src and font-src (CSP_BLOCKS, naming each directive and origin to add, and whether in the header or webapp@csp-append). Refuses a caller without the permission (PERMISSION_DENIED) and an unknown provider.

A postal code's place from the local Geo data (plans/archive/Maps.md §6.1, §6.3; GeoDataServices imports it), for a map, a search and an address with no point: country and code only, no street address, party or outside request. The country is a Geo ID or an ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 code; the code is read by the importer's rules (normalize#PostalCode: leading zeros kept, a US ZIP+4 read as its ZIP code). Each match is the code's active representative point (the in-date GPR_REPRESENTATIVE association of lowest priority: in the US the Census ZCTA point before GeoNames'), never a user-confirmed point or a record's own location, with a broad extent around it (not the area's boundary), its precision (precisionText "Approximate location — postal area"), its source, edition and attribution, and its place names, which are aliases of the one area. A full code with no row falls back to its country's declared prefix (Canada, Great Britain, the Netherlands) at a lower precision (matchKind prefix, GPP_PLACE_ESTIMATE); no other country's code is cut. ambiguous is true when there is more than one match or a code has several place names, which are choices, none chosen. No match is matches empty with reasonCode NO_MATCH; a country that is not one COUNTRY_UNKNOWN; text that is no code of the country CODE_INVALID, with reason. Cached in maps.postal.lookup (bounded), which an import clears. Reads public reference data only, changes nothing: every signed-in user may call it (MAPS_DIALOG), as an adapter or the local-map dialog does.

parameter.name: matches
parameter.description: Each {geoId, countryGeoId, normalizedCode, displayCode, granularityEnumId, matchKind (code or prefix), lon, lat, extent [west, south, east, north], precisionEnumId, precisionText, approximate, dataSetId, sourceKey, publisher, edition, attribution, licenseName, sourceText, placeNames [{name, adminName1, adminName2, sourceKey, lon, lat}]}

service.description: The maps.geodata readiness provider (data/AdminConfigurationData.xml), changing nothing, for a caller with ADMIN_OVERVIEW_VIEW (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise): postal data in date for the instance's default country (the country of instance@default-locale; GEO_DATA_MISSING), the last run of each imported scope did not fail (IMPORT_FAILED, naming the data set and country), and a data set covering that country has its license acknowledged (LICENSE_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED, while no Geo data is there to look up).

Add a geographic file (GeoJSON, TopoJSON, EsriJSON, GPX, KML, GML, WKT, WKB, CSV with a WKT, WKB or latitude and longitude column, or a zipped shapefile) as one of the signed-in user's map overlays: an upload (file), kept as it was sent in Maps/overlays of their personal drive (a name already there gets "name (2).ext"), or a file of a drive they read (driveId, path), which stays where it is. The file is read first (MapSourceServices.convert#Overlay: at most maps@overlay-max-bytes within maps@import-max-bytes, at most maps@max-features features (5000 when that is 0), WGS84 or a declared EPSG:3857 (another CRS is refused until reprojection is built), at most 4 MiB of characters as GeoJSON) and, when it cannot be drawn, refused with nothing written (FORMAT_UNKNOWN, TOO_LARGE, NOT_PARSED, NOT_FORMAT, CRS_UNSUPPORTED, TOO_MANY_FEATURES, NO_FEATURES, TOO_LARGE_TO_DRAW; NOT_FOUND for a file the user does not read). A feature whose geometry is not sane is left out and counted (rejectedCount, notes), as is what is not read (network links, icons, styles, extended data). Records a moqui.maps.MapOverlay row of the user's (the same file again brings its row up to date), at most 100 (TOO_MANY_OVERLAYS). Sharing it is sharing the file in Files. A file too large to draw whole (TOO_MANY_FEATURES, TOO_LARGE_TO_DRAW) is refused with canGeneralize true; with generalize true it is kept and simplified on the server into vector tiles beside it (MapSourceServices build#OverlayTiles in the MapOverlayTiles ServiceJob, generalizing true; a file the user may not write beside is TILES_NOT_WRITABLE, one being simplified now TILES_RUNNING).

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: An uploaded file

parameter.name: generalize
parameter.description: Simplify a file too large to draw whole into vector tiles on the server

service.description: Remove one of the signed-in user's overlays from their maps: the row only, the file stays in its drive. Another user's overlay, and one that is not there, are RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

The signed-in user's overlays (their saved places among them, isPlaces) and, read-only, other users' overlays whose file the user may read now in its drive (a share of the file or a folder above it, or a membership: FileServices get#DriveAccess), at most 100 of each. Each has its layerId (overlay:ID), label, owner, file name (its path only for one's own), format, feature count, rejected count, bounds, notes and the overlay transition's URL; one simplified into vector tiles its tilesStatus, tilesProgress and tilesNote, and when ready its tileUrl (LocalMap's tile transition) and tilesMaxZoom. Changes nothing.

An overlay's file as sanitized GeoJSON, for Browse's overlay transition on every request: the current user must read the file in its drive now (the owner as any reader: a revoked share or a removed member is refused at the next request), writing nothing (no ResourceRecent). Not there, or not readable, is OVERLAY_MISSING (404); a file gone FILE_GONE (404); a file that no longer reads as an overlay 422 with its reason, one grown past 4 MiB of GeoJSON 413 (TOO_LARGE_TO_DRAW). Cached by the file's version in maps.overlay.geojson, the 413 too.

One of the signed-in user's own overlays to edit on the map (P4b; MapOverlays.js editOverlay): its sanitized GeoJSON as a map draws it, the version of its file (version, which a save names) and where a save writes (editPath; inPlace true only when a save over the file changes nothing of it but the edit: a GeoJSON file that is exactly what the converter makes of it, the user's places, or an edited copy; else the edit is written beside it as name.edited.geojson and the original kept). Refused: another user's overlay or none (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE), one simplified into tiles (NOT_EDITABLE), a file the user may not write or add a file beside (NOT_WRITABLE), a file gone (FILE_GONE) or no longer drawn (the reader's reason, TOO_LARGE_TO_DRAW). Writes nothing.

Save an edit of one of the signed-in user's own overlays (P4b; MapOverlays.js saveEdit): geojson, a FeatureCollection, read by MapSourceServices.convert#Overlay as any overlay is (its bounds, maps@max-features, plain-text labels and descriptions, nothing else of a feature kept) and written through FileServices.save#Text as the user (the drive's write check, quota and versions) to the overlay's file when get#OverlayEdit's rule holds for the file as it is now, else beside it as name.edited.geojson (upload#Resource, keepBoth: no file replaced), which the overlay then draws (sourcePath, sourceCrs and importNotes keep the original's). The overlay's row is locked, and the save refused when the file is not the version the edit started from (baseVersion: STALE_VERSION). Refused as get#OverlayEdit refuses, and: not a FeatureCollection (NOT_FORMAT), no feature (NO_FEATURES, saved places excepted), a geometry that is not valid (INVALID_GEOMETRY, with notes), past what a map draws (TOO_LARGE_TO_DRAW, TOO_MANY_FEATURES), a saved place that is not a point (POINTS_ONLY).

Save a named point to the signed-in user's places: Maps/places.geojson of their personal drive (written through FileServices save#Text, so the drive's versions keep each change), listed as their overlay "My places". The user's places row is locked first, so two saves at once are one after the other. Refused: no name (LABEL_MISSING), a point out of range (POINT_INVALID), a places file that is not a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of at most maps@overlay-max-bytes (PLACES_UNREADABLE: it is never overwritten), 1000 places or maps@max-features (TOO_MANY_PLACES). Private until the user shares the file (or its folder) in Files.
Remove one of the signed-in user's saved places by its ID; one that is not theirs is RECORD_UNAVAILABLE.

Candidate places for a text from one configured geocoder (plans/archive/Maps.md §6.1, §6.2, §8): the provider named, or the enabled geocoder (a MapProvider of a kind under MPK_GEOCODER: the US Census geocoder, a self-hosted Nominatim or Photon, or this server's own index of Overture address points, MPK_GEOCODER_OVERTURE) that passed its test as it is configured now and may be asked now (an outside one with outside requests on, the local one while a region's addresses are active), first by sequenceNum. The local geocoder sends nothing: its candidates are address matches (GPP_ADDRESS_MATCH, the point's position kind not stated), a number found without its suffix or a street (GPP_PLACE_ESTIMATE), each with its source dataset, license, GERS ID and release; a text it does not match is answered with the postal area of the code read from it (NO_ADDRESS_MATCH, approximate) or none (NO_MATCH). Each candidate is {label (plain text), lon, lat, matchKind (address, street, postal, place), precisionEnumId and precisionText (the Census geocoder's: an address placed by street-range interpolation, GPP_STREET_RANGE, never a rooftop; an address point GPP_ADDRESS_MATCH; a postal code GPP_POSTAL_AREA; a street or place GPP_PLACE_ESTIMATE), extent}; several are ambiguous, choices with none chosen; with the provider's name, attribution and terms. Refused, nothing sent: outside requests off (EXTERNAL_REQUESTS_OFF), no enabled tested geocoder (NO_GEOCODER), a text of fewer than 2 or more than 200 characters (QUERY_INVALID), a country the geocoder does not cover (COUNTRY_NOT_COVERED, the Census geocoder outside the US), a provider whose allowedOperations name neither geocode nor search (OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED), the provider's rate passed (RATE_LIMITED: requestsPerSecond, 1 for Nominatim and Photon when empty, claimed atomically on each server by itself) and its requests a day not used up (DAILY_LIMIT: requestsPerDay, a calendar day in UTC, claimed on its MapProviderDayCount row for the whole cluster). One GET with no credentials, following no redirect, ten seconds, the body read to at most 1 MiB whatever its Content-Length, to no internal address unless the provider is allowed the private network; a failure is PROVIDER_FAILED, naming the provider, and no other outside service is asked. This server keeps an answer only for cachePolicy shared (private is the browser's alone), for cacheSeconds or the answer's own max-age, by a digest, never the text. Called only by an explicit search: no map, record or dialog calls it on opening.
